record.original_question: For the DNA alignment example whose model M is the set of positive 4×4 matrices (pij) of rank at most 2 and whose likelihood function is L = (∏i pii)^4 · (∏i≠j pij)^2 · (∑i,j pij)^−40, is the matrix (1/40)·[[3,3,2,2],[3,3,2,2],[2,2,3,3],[2,2,3,3]] a global maximum of L?

evidence.quote: Here the model M consists of all (positive) 4×4-matrices (pij ) of rank at most two. In the given alignment, each match occurs four times and each mismatch occurs two times. Hence the likelihood function (3.1) equals L = (∏i pii)^4 · (∏i≠j pij)^2 · (∑i,j pij)^−40.
Based on experiments with the EM algorithm, we conjectured that the matrix (pˆij) = 1/40 [[3, 3, 2, 2], [3, 3, 2, 2], [2, 2, 3, 3], [2, 2, 3, 3]] is a global maximum of the likelihood function L.
I offered a cash prize of 100 Swiss Francs for the resolution of this very specific conjecture, and this prize remains unclaimed and is still available at this time (August 2007).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ denote the set of all positive $4\times 4$ matrices $P=(p_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le 4}$ (i.e., $p_{ij}>0$) of rank at most $2$. Consider the likelihood function $L:M\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ defined by
$$L(P) \;=\; \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^{4} p_{ii}\Bigr)^{4} \cdot \Bigl(\prod_{i\ne j} p_{ij}\Bigr)^{2} \cdot \Bigl(\sum_{i,j=1}^{4} p_{ij}\Bigr)^{-40}.$$
Decide whether the matrix
$$\widehat{P} \;=\; \frac{1}{40}\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 3 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 3 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$$
is a global maximum of $L$ on $M$.
artifact.category_tag: algebraic statistics / maximum likelihood on rank-constrained matrices
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (the "100 Swiss Francs problem") was resolved affirmatively by Mingfu Zhu (with co-authors), with the resolution appearing in "Solving the 100 Swiss Francs Problem," Mathematics in Computer Science (2011). The given matrix is confirmed to be the global maximum of the likelihood function on the rank-2 model.

status_evidence.title: Solving the 100 Swiss Francs Problem - Mathematics in Computer Science
status_evidence.snippet: In 2005, the third author offered a cash prize of 100 Swiss Francs for the solution of a particular 4×4-instance that was described in a DNA sequence alignment example... the maximum value occurring at P(a, b).
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture was confirmed; the matrix is the global maximum.

status_evidence.title: Maximum Likelihood for Matrices with Rank Constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the rank-2 likelihood model including the 4x4 case originally posed as the 100 Swiss Francs problem.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work treats the resolved 100 Swiss Francs problem as a known result.
